title: Fold SparseTensorEntry evidence digest sort fallback into one validation pass
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: SparseTensorEntry already retained an exact canonical evidence_sha256s tuple by object identity, but an out-of-order exact tuple was validated only until the first inversion and then routed through _sorted_strings(..., digests=True). That fallback revalidated the complete bounded sequence, allocated a second converted list and duplicate-detection set, sorted, and materialized the canonical tuple. Adding an evidence index, cache, adapter, or second evidence representation would increase rather than reduce the surface.
primary_claim: SparseTensorEntry now validates evidence digests and detects canonical ordering in one bounded traversal. Exact already-canonical tuples retain object identity; non-canonical and non-tuple bounded sequences are validated once, sorted only when required, and duplicate-refused by adjacent comparison. Empty, invalid, duplicate, and oversized evidence inputs remain fail closed. Fourfold authority, TensorView wire semantics, evidence digest semantics, projection status semantics, and provenance binding are unchanged.
gardener_decision: Remove the redundant _sorted_strings fallback from the tensor evidence path and fold canonicalization into the existing bounded traversal. The exact evidence tuple remains the single immutable representation; only inputs that actually require ordering allocate a temporary list for sorting. This removes duplicate validation and duplicate-detection-set work without broadening the Tensor/Fourfold architecture.
acceptance: an unsorted exact evidence digest tuple is canonicalized deterministically while every digest receives _sha256 validation exactly once
an exact already-canonical evidence digest tuple remains eligible for object-identity reuse through the existing SparseTensorEntry contract
